correctness.rationale: Independence of the n−1 square representatives makes the product of distinct basis vectors vanish coefficientwise. In every singleton coordinate exactly one column is nonzero; the singleton rows must use distinct columns by invertibility. The other two columns span U and are B-orthogonal, so neither is isotropic and the nondegenerate B forces all remaining U-components to vanish. Perpendicularity is an involution of q+1 projective lines with exactly 2 or 0 fixed points in odd characteristic according to −λ, and exactly 1 in even characteristic by bijectivity of squaring. A nonzero v_i receives one target coordinate precisely on its own nonisotropic orbit; hit orbits are separated by their nonempty disjoint one-arrow index sets, while all unhit orbits coincide in support. The two sources in U have identical support and the singleton-target supports are fixed, so the count survives the common swap and is for the whole marked graph. Choosing u_1=e_1 and u_i=e_i+v_i on distinct remaining orbits makes t=min(n−1,N) with independence automatic. This proves the maximum, including N=1; the F5 example has the stated distinct outdegree multisets.
residual_risks: The frozen checker covers only selected prime fields and extremal witnesses; the separate F4 check is finite. The proof, not these checks, gives every prime power and dimension. No classification of unmarked isomorphism classes or arbitrary corank-one dependencies is established.

evidence: Boudi et al. give a general rank-one-square block structure, block basis changes and the bilinear form criterion for extending a natural family.
Alshatnawi et al. establish invariance of graph balance, allowing the associated graphs themselves to vary.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither theorem classifies the zero coordinates of all independent square representatives in varying orthogonal frames, or establishes the attainable number of distinct marked adjacency patterns.

evidence: Known orthogonal moduli provide at most N basis choices, not a lower bound when many frames give identical graph support.
The two-dimensional count has no issue of selecting several independent square directions that simultaneously maximize orbit hits.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A sharp min(n,N) needs both the separation/collapse mechanism on the entire projection list and a realization satisfying independence; it is not the N bound specialized, nor the graph count for an isolated binary block applied independently to different sources.

evidence: Natural-basis changes in this stratum reduce to orthogonal frames on one block, hence to projective perpendicular-line pairs after scaling and swapping.
Question 14 is about natural-basis classes, not their image in support patterns; Question 30 asks about simultaneous graph realization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Basis classes and marked support classes are not equivalent: when two or more orbits are unhit they all have the same support. The hit/unhit quotient by the projected square lines, not just the parametrization, supplies the count.

evidence: The October 25 binary graph-spectrum finding assumes dim E²=1, not dim E²=n−1 for n≥3.

The November 2 all-field two-dimensional finding has the same isotropic-line mechanism but only one distinct source square and no singleton blocks; the other November 2 comparison is binary square-rank-one.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: These are genuine adjacent graph-spectrum records, but none enumerates the aggregate support across independently marked sources in the assigned stratum. Later record dates are not evidence of earlier priority.

originality.rationale: The structural block theorem and orthogonal parametrization are prior results, and the projective basis count follows by a fixed-point calculation. The supported distinct claim is the marked graph-support spectrum for a sole square-dependence pair with independent representatives, and its sharp extremum over realizable algebras. The strongest inspected comparisons do not cover that classification.
residual_risks: A bounded literature and catalogue comparison cannot rule out an unindexed equivalent graph-support enumeration. No priority claim is made for the orthogonal block parametrization or the projective fixed-point count.

value.rationale: The graph of an evolution algebra depends on its natural basis. On a minimal nontrivial dependence stratum, the invariant specifies exactly which basis moduli genuinely change the graph, including when different moduli collapse to one marked pattern. The attained bound limits simultaneous marked realizations by both dimension and field size, independently of the sizes of the basis-change groups. This is a useful complete classification in the direction of the survey questions, not a solution to unrestricted graph realization.
residual_risks: Removing the marking can identify distinct patterns; no general unmarked count follows.
